modules.name: Idler and magneto drives
modules.purpose: Crank gear drives the idler; the idler drives both magneto gears. Key 12 is an assembly: the separate accessory wheel, bushing and attaching screws also matter.
modules.method: Reuse the solved involute profile and linked extrusion for the spur gears. Use native revolved/cylindrical steps for shaft/pin, spline cuts for take-offs, and separate bushings, bearing seats, seals and coupling retainers.
modules.evidence: Resolve applicable tooth counts, modules, shaft centres and axial planes. H magneto speed is 1.5 times crank speed. The H vacuum accessory speed is 1.14 times crank speed: resolve the compound-idler/accessory-pad route rather than put every take-off at magneto speed.
modules.checks: Close all shared gear ratios/centres/phases; measure pin/bushing fits, bearing support, spline engagement and endplay. Check screws and coupling retainers as full envelopes.
modules.legacy: The separate accessory study supplies spur-gear/phase and coupling methods. Its relocated axes and illustrative dimensions are not engine datums.

modules.name: Fuel-pump gear and coupling
modules.effort: Low to medium; about 1-2 iterations after variant decision
modules.purpose: The smaller wheel attached to the cam gear drives key 22. The wheel already exists; its driven partner and pump-side coupling do not.
modules.method: Use the shared spur-gear declaration, linked outline extrusion, stepped shaft, coupling socket, seal/bushing and native retaining features. Add the pump mounting interface as a separate assembly.
modules.evidence: Choose the applicable old or replacement H pump installation. C-3-6 says the replacement changes the drive gear, adds a coupling and changes stud extension from 1.31 to 0.75 inch. Confirm drive ratio, coupling form, pad datum and endplay before final gear dimensions.
modules.checks: Whole-pitch tooth clearance, shaft/bushing fit, positive coupling engagement, axial capture, seal and complete stud/nut clearance.
modules.legacy: Reuse general gear/shaft/seat construction. Do not carry an older illustrative fuel-pump marker into the H engine as a finished pump.

modules.name: Oil, tachometer and scavenge drive
modules.purpose: The cam-gear spline drives the oil/tach shaft. Oil and scavenge gears need their paired pumping chambers, supports and a distinct tachometer take-off.
modules.method: Use linked involute gears and native stepped shafts with matching splines/keyways. Derive close-fitting gear chambers and covers from rotating envelopes; retain separate bushings, relief/bypass parts and the tach bevel pair.
modules.evidence: Our CamshaftGear/CamClusterGear currently have plain radius-9.55 mm bores, not the documented oil/tach spline receiver. A-4-16 expands the branch into 52 callouts. Its separate tach bevel gears resolve a basic-text ambiguity that calls key 11 a tach drive although A-4-8 names it the scavenge driver. Read original limits for tip/end clearance and shaft fits.
modules.checks: Matching spline and axial engagement; both pump meshes; gear-tip and end clearance; supported shafts; open suction/discharge/return routes. An open static path does not establish pumping performance.
modules.legacy: Old pump and accessory scenes are references for construction only. Their illustrative dimensions and previously documented pump overlaps require fresh native modelling and checks.

modules.name: Governor bevel drive
modules.effort: High for a correct pair; about 2-3 iterations
modules.purpose: A keyed gear at the front of the camshaft turns the governor shaft across the cam axis. The case also needs the guide/support and oil-fed governor pad.
modules.method: Test compatible bevel teeth on intersecting pitch cones with a shared apex. FCGear bevel code is a candidate: it lofts compatible tooth sections and exposes pitch angle/module/backlash. Use keyed native shaft and separate bushing/retention; preserve the cam journal.
modules.evidence: H governor speed is 0.809 times crank speed. With a half-speed cam this implies about 1.618 governor/cam speed. For a confirmed 90-degree shaft angle, the corresponding pitch cones would be about 58.3/31.7 degrees; two default 45-degree cones would give the wrong ratio. These are derived constraints, not recovered OEM tooth counts. Confirm axis angle, cone apex, face width, key and shaft stations.
modules.checks: First prove the unequal-cone bevel method in a small saved/reopened and parameter-mutated fixture with STEP. FCGear uses Python proxies: pin/carry that dependency if adopted, or implement reviewed linked native profiles in our backend. Then check pitch-cone closure, phase/backlash, tooth-pitch interference, guide fit and oil-pad routing.
modules.legacy: Our tested spur extrusion is useful for hubs, not proof of a bevel mesh. FCGear was not found in the inspected standard Mod folders; installation/adoption has not been tested.

modules.name: Starter shaftgear and simplified shell
modules.effort: Medium initially; about 1-2 interface build/validation iterations
modules.purpose: User-selected initial scope: model key21, which meshes with the crankshaft gear, with its shaft/support interfaces. Represent motor/adapter/internal contents by one simplified shell. Keys17-20 are intentionally deferred internal mechanisms.
modules.method: Reuse the solved involute profile and linked native extrusion for the crank-to-starter shaftgear mesh; add the supported stepped shaft and essential locating interfaces. Form one coarse native shell with correctly located mount, shaft opening and clear internal cavity. Keep the external gear and shaft as a separate rotating part; do not fuse them into the stationary shell.
modules.evidence: Verify applicable module/tooth count, mesh centre/axial plane, backlash, phase, shaft/bearing fit and mounting datum; unsupported dimensions stay marked estimates. The H 32:1 starter ratio is an eventual internal-transmission constraint, not implemented by this shell. Accurate main-train engagement does not establish the unmodelled worm/clutch mechanism.
modules.checks: Check the complete external spur pitch, shaft/support fit, axial capture, bearing/case stock and the hollow shell clearances against all new/changed neighbours. Save/reopen and strict STEP remain required. Do not imply torque transmission or starting engagement through the simplified internals. A genuine worm/wheel/clutch fixture is needed only when those internals are rebuilt later.
modules.legacy: Reuse the earlier spur-mesh, stepped-shaft and seating methods. Do not transplant the relocated teaching layout. Its worm deliberately clears a spur-like wheel and remains unsuitable for the later detailed reconstruction.

additional_gaps.name: Oil/tach receiver on existing cam gear
additional_gaps.work: Reconstruct the rear hub and matching female spline together with key8. Preserve existing gear attachment and cam journal; a plain through-hole is insufficient.

additional_gaps.name: Front crankshaft face gear and alternator coupling
additional_gaps.status: Outside the 25-key diagram; not in current engine
additional_gaps.work: Add the separate crankshaft face gear and its attaching screws/tab locks, then the mating alternator gear/coupling, thrust washer, shaft/bearing and mounting pad. The manual locates this on the crankshaft, not the propeller shaft. H alternator speed is 3 times crank speed. Face/crown teeth require a dedicated compatible-mesh fixture; cosmetic teeth on the propeller gear would be the wrong design.
additional_gaps.source: A-4-20 PDF38 keys21-23; A-4-33 PDF46; A-12-10 printed A-12-4 / PDF80; torque table PDF100; H PDF153

additional_gaps.name: Tachometer bevel gears and output shaft
additional_gaps.work: Use A-4-16 keys24/47/45 to separate the tachometer bevel take-off from the scavenge spur pair, with its housing, seal and retaining parts. H tach speed is 0.5 times crank speed.

additional_gaps.name: Compound idler, accessory pads and supports
additional_gaps.status: Key12 is an assembly, not one wheel
additional_gaps.work: Include the second accessory wheel, screws/bushing, support pin and case bores. Resolve each H take-off ratio and applicable pad before locating magnetos or vacuum pumps.

additional_gaps.name: Pump bodies, valves and oil routes
additional_gaps.status: Gear outlines alone would leave the mechanism incomplete
additional_gaps.work: Provide both pump chambers, bushings, covers, relief/bypass parts, inlet/outlet interfaces and supported oil routes. Hidden galleries require reference evidence.

additional_gaps.name: Starter shell and main-train interface
additional_gaps.status: Initial simplification explicitly selected by user
additional_gaps.work: Preserve the external shaftgear mesh, supported shaft and mount/clearance interfaces; keep a separate stationary shell enclosing simplified internals. Worm gears, clutch spring, internal bearings/damper and detailed retention stay deferred. The OEM functional path remains reference information, not a simulated transmission through the shell.
additional_gaps.source: User scope decision 2026-10-13; A-4-15 PDF32; A-11-6 PDF74
